payload.reason: The evidence indicates a correlation between daytime activity and socioeconomic status (SEC), suggesting that people active during the day tend to have higher SEC and use more standard language.

claims.text: People active during the day have higher average income and use more standard language compared to those active at night.
Standard language use is more prevalent during the daytime, while non-standard variants are predominant at night, indicating a link to socioeconomic status.
Higher socioeconomic status is associated with the use of more standard language, which correlates with daytime activity patterns.
